source_pin_scope.rule: Every dependency selector, resolution, live detector source, source gate, R1 baseline, ADR, capability authority and baseline authority used by this corpus is pinned.

source_pins.role: optional regex dependency selector and metrics feature gate
live custom-first incumbent regex redaction pipeline, four disabled bounded scanner implementations retained for equivalence tests, detector order, tokens and allocation-free Luhn join
R1 capability and historical detector baseline

post_capture_provenance_refresh.no_claim_boundary: This refresh classifies one shared baseline pin drift and records the current content hash. The five added top-level objects belong to independent Phase-2 static audits, while the CAP-REGEX-PRIVACY and CAP-LAB-DETERMINISM rows remain byte-equivalent after canonicalization. It does not execute the R2.1 contract, change any corpus vector or dispatch rule, implement a scanner, prove performance or protection, authorize dependency exit or cutover, close the tracker, or establish broad workspace health.

provenance.method: Synthetic values, expected UTF-8 byte spans and outcomes were authored from the published detector languages and boundary rules without generating expected rows from the incumbent engine.
provenance.incumbent_use: The incumbent is applied only after authorship as a differential oracle.

provenance.method: Synthetic cases expand the R1 eleven-row detector baseline with exact spans and missing boundary classes.
provenance.incumbent_use: R1 is historical provenance, not the sole specification.

provenance.method: Synthetic minimum, common and maximum-length card candidates were selected against the right-to-left Luhn mod-10 rule before differential comparison.
provenance.incumbent_use: The private production Luhn helper is not used to generate expected validity.

provenance.method: ASCII word, Unicode word, emoji, separator, adjacency and no-sliding-window rows were hand-authored against Unicode word-boundary and UTF-8 byte-offset semantics.
provenance.incumbent_use: Observed disagreements fail the future fast path closed to the incumbent.

rollback_triggers: Any changed expected span, candidate validity, detector order or whole-value token
Any custom, drifted, unrecognized or conflicting identity entering the built-in allowset
Any scanner returning a partial result instead of falling through on disagreement
Any accepted detector configuration losing incumbent fallback
Any source pin or capability authority drift without reviewed corpus refresh
no_claim_boundaries: R2.1 freezes incumbent built-in detector and whole-value redaction behavior but implements no scanner or fast path.
The corpus does not authorize changing or removing regex, dispatching custom patterns to built-in scanners, or production cutover.
The corpus does not claim exhaustive detection, absence of false positives or false negatives, or complete privacy protection.
Observed acceptance and rejection rows are compatibility facts and are not declarations that every behavior is desirable.
All spans are half-open UTF-8 byte offsets, not Unicode scalar, code-point, display-column or grapheme indexes.
The corpus does not prove production multi-signal privacy wiring or protection of log bodies, resource attributes, identifiers or event names.
The corpus does not prove latency, throughput, allocation, memory, cancellation, denial-of-service resistance or performance parity.
All values are synthetic and the corpus proves nothing about handling real secrets or personal data.
The corpus does not prove broad workspace health, release readiness, live RCH fleet availability, or local Cargo fallback approval.
The corpus does not authorize tracker closure, dependency exit, file deletion, or cancellation of peer work.
